sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: I want you to conjure an image in your mind of the white stripes.
sentences.zh: 我想请你在脑海中勾勒出白色标线的样子。

sentences.en: Not those white stripes, but the white stripes that divide the lanes of traffic going in the same direction on a major highway.
sentences.zh: 不是那种“白条纹”（乐队），而是高速公路上分隔同向车道的白色标线。

sentences.en: How long are those stripes?
sentences.zh: 那些标线有多长？

sentences.en: You can spread your arms out to estimate if you want to.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，可以张开双臂估算一下。

sentences.en: Over the course of many years, a psychology researcher named Dennis Schaefer at Ohio State
sentences.zh: 多年来，俄亥俄州立大学的一位心理学研究员丹尼斯·谢弗（Dennis Schaefer）

sentences.en: asked students from many different parts of the country this question.
sentences.zh: 向全国各地的学生提出了这个问题。

sentences.en: And the most common response was two feet.
sentences.zh: 最常见的回答是两英尺。

sentences.en: So if you're like most people, you estimated that those white stripes are two feet long, maybe a little more.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你和大多数人一样，你估计那些白色标线长两英尺，或许再多一点。

sentences.en: But if you did, you'd be very, very wrong.
sentences.zh: 但如果你这么想，那就大错特错了。

sentences.en: This is Tom Vanderbilt.
sentences.zh: 这位是汤姆·范德比尔特（Tom Vanderbilt）。

sentences.en: My name is Tom Vanderbilt.
sentences.zh: 我叫汤姆·范德比尔特。

sentences.en: I'm a writer in New York and author of Traffic, Why We Drive the Way We Do, and What It Says About Us.
sentences.zh: 我是纽约的一名作家，著有《交通：我们为何这样开车，以及它说明了什么》一书。

sentences.en: Every three pages of Tom's terrific book, Traffic, I could probably turn into a 99% Invisible episode.
sentences.zh: 汤姆那本精彩的《交通》书，我大概每三页就能改编成一期《99%隐形》节目。

sentences.en: But back to the highway.
sentences.zh: 但还是回到高速公路的话题上。

sentences.en: Well, early on in my research, I was talking to a highway engineer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在研究初期，我曾与一位公路工程师交谈。

sentences.en: And he said if your car is ever broken down on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果你的车在路边抛锚了。

sentences.en: If you've ever been forced to get out of your vehicle on a highway.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经被迫在高速公路上走出车外。

sentences.en: Just take a moment to notice what a strange landscape it is.
sentences.zh: 花点时间留意一下，那是一个多么奇怪的景观。

sentences.en: If you happen to be standing near a road sign, these road signs are huge.
sentences.zh: 如果你恰好站在路牌附近，会发现这些路牌非常巨大。

sentences.en: I mean, they're not meant to be experienced as humans on foot.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们并不是为了让步行的人去体验的。

sentences.en: They're meant to be experienced at 75 miles an hour.
sentences.zh: 它们是为了让人们在时速75英里的情况下体验的。

sentences.en: With a clear view typeface.
sentences.zh: 使用Clearview字体。

sentences.en: Perfectly visible, retro-reflective.
sentences.zh: 清晰可见，具有反光效果。

sentences.en: And then there are the white stripes.
sentences.zh: 然后就是那些白色标线。

sentences.en: If you actually kind of got out of your car and were able to walk on a closed highway and walk from one end of those stripes to the other,
sentences.zh: 如果你真的走出车外，能够走上一条封闭的高速公路，并从这些标线的一端走到另一端，

sentences.en: you'd find that, I mean, years ago in the United States, the highway standard was 15 feet long, which is longer than a car itself.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，我的意思是，多年前在美国，高速公路的标准是15英尺长，比汽车本身还要长。

sentences.en: Current Federal Highway Administration guidelines suggest a length of 10 feet with 30 feet between the dashes.
sentences.zh: 现行的联邦公路管理局指南建议标线长度为10英尺，间距为30英尺。

sentences.en: That's something that is shocking to people.
sentences.zh: 这让人们感到震惊。

sentences.en: And remember, most people in the Schaefer study said that those stripes were two feet long.
sentences.zh: 记住，谢弗研究中的大多数人说那些标线只有两英尺长。

sentences.en: That's such a vast gulf there between, it's not, you know, it's not sort of like, you know, they're actually five feet.
sentences.zh: 这中间存在巨大的鸿沟，这不像是因为，你知道，它们实际上有五英尺长。

sentences.en: We thought they were two, you know, margin of error kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我们以为是两英尺，你知道，这属于误差范围之类的东西。

sentences.en: And it goes back to this fundamental point that when you're in a car at high speeds, you're experiencing only a sense of the landscape rather than the actual landscape.
sentences.zh: 这归结为一个基本点：当你以高速驾车时，你体验到的只是对景观的一种感觉，而不是真实的景观。

sentences.en: This kind of sense of the landscape has been presented to you to essentially make you feel comfortable.
sentences.zh: 这种景观感呈现给你，本质上是为了让你感到舒适。

sentences.en: And to make a highway work at what are really evolutionarily ridiculous speeds for a human to travel.
sentences.zh: 并让高速公路在人类演化史上极其荒谬的速度下运作。

sentences.en: You have this big, flat, wide open, you know, kind of stretch of road that even if you have a 65 mile an hour sign,
sentences.zh: 你拥有宽阔、平坦、开阔的路段，即使限速牌写着65英里每小时，

sentences.en: the message of the road is telling you something entirely different.
sentences.zh: 道路传达的信息却完全不同。

sentences.en: And I think that's really where a lot of our behavior comes from.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是我们许多行为的根源所在。

sentences.en: Sometimes, you know, you have sort of willful speeding, willful kind of lawbreaking.
sentences.zh: 有时，你知道，会有某种蓄意的超速，蓄意的违规。

sentences.en: But a lot of it is just people are paying attention to the visual messaging of the road, not to their speedometer.
sentences.zh: 但很大程度上是因为人们关注的是道路的视觉信息，而不是车速表。

sentences.en: Long dividing lines and clear vistas give the illusion that you're going at a reasonable speed.
sentences.zh: 长长的分隔线和开阔的视野会给人一种你正在以合理速度行驶的错觉。

sentences.en: As soon as something encroaches into view, you get a sense of how fast you're going.
sentences.zh: 一旦有东西进入视野，你就能感觉到自己开得有多快。

sentences.en: That's one reason why those temporary concrete walls that crews put up right next to the road during construction are so unnerving.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么施工期间工人在路边放置的临时混凝土墙如此令人不安的原因之一。

sentences.en: The error in perception of white stripe length is attributed to the fact that when we drive on the highway,
sentences.zh: 对白色标线长度的感知错误归因于这样一个事实：当我们行驶在高速公路上时，

sentences.en: we tend to look so far ahead that we usually only experience the dashes and gaps when they are very far away and at an angle where they look shorter.
sentences.zh: 我们往往看得太远，以至于通常只有在标线和间隙非常遥远，且处于看起来较短的角度时，才会体验到它们。

sentences.en: But there's no consensus as to why people all over the country were so consistently wrong with the two feet estimate.
sentences.zh: 但对于为什么全国各地的人在两英尺的估计上如此一致地出错，目前还没有共识。

sentences.en: It's become my favorite, one of my favorite cocktail party, you know, facts.
sentences.zh: 这已经成了我最喜欢的鸡尾酒会谈资之一。

sentences.en: Mine too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: Stump the driver with this white stripes information.
sentences.zh: 用这个关于白色标线的知识去考考司机吧。

sentences.en: I don't want to leave you with the impression that the white dividing lines are uniform, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我不想让你留下白色分隔线是统一的印象。

sentences.en: You won't find, you know, 10-foot highway lines on, say, a boulevard in New York City.
sentences.zh: 你不会在纽约市的林荫大道上找到10英尺长的高速公路标线。

sentences.en: And you probably won't find 10 or 15-foot stripes on bridges or highway on-ramps.
sentences.zh: 你可能也不会在桥梁或高速公路入口匝道上找到10或15英尺长的标线。

sentences.en: Or let's hope you don't, because that's kind of an entirely inappropriate design language for that space.
sentences.zh: 或者说我们希望你找不到，因为那对于那个空间来说是一种完全不合适的设计语言。

sentences.en: Limited access highways are designed for a very precise purpose.
sentences.zh: 限制进入的高速公路是为非常精确的目的而设计的。

sentences.en: There's, the highway's meant for uninterrupted, fast-flowing traffic.
sentences.zh: 高速公路旨在实现不间断、快速流动的交通。

sentences.en: Get people from point A to point B as quickly as possible with no interruptions.
sentences.zh: 让人尽可能快地从A点到达B点，且没有任何中断。

sentences.en: I mean, that sort of environment does not work in cities or suburbs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种环境在城市或郊区是行不通的。

sentences.en: The problem is when that approach is grafted into places where it doesn't belong.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当这种方法被移植到不属于它的地方时。

sentences.en: I think we're actually kind of paying the price for this right now in some suburban environments
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在在一些郊区环境中正为此付出代价，

sentences.en: where you find these kind of arterial highways that were built almost to a highway engineering standard
sentences.zh: 在那里你会发现这些动脉公路几乎是按照高速公路工程标准建造的，

sentences.en: with, again, these long sight lines, wide roads, encouraging people to go faSt.
sentences.zh: 同样有着长长的视线、宽阔的道路，鼓励人们开得很快。

sentences.en: And then we went and built all kinds of development along those arterial highways,
sentences.zh: 然后我们又在这些动脉公路沿线进行了各种开发，

sentences.en: which was never really supposed to be there.
sentences.zh: 而这些地方本不该有这些开发。

sentences.en: But with so many people driving on these roads, they became absolutely irresistible to commerce.
sentences.zh: 但随着在这些道路上行驶的人越来越多，它们对商业来说变得绝对无法抗拒。

sentences.en: This is kind of the new American main street, right, where you have your Costco's and your fast food
sentences.zh: 这算是新的美国主街，对吧，那里有Costco和快餐店，

sentences.en: and all sorts of in-and-out parking lots, driveways, drive-thrus, yet people also going very faSt.
sentences.zh: 还有各种进进出出的停车场、车道、免下车服务，但人们的车速依然非常快。

sentences.en: And a guy named Eric Dunbaugh does a lot of research suggesting that these are really some of the most dangerous places
sentences.zh: 一个叫埃里克·邓博（Eric Dunbaugh）的人做了大量研究，表明这些地方实际上是美国目前

sentences.en: to currently drive in America, not crowded urban cities, which is what a lot of people would think.
sentences.zh: 开车最危险的地方，而不是许多人认为的拥挤的城市中心。

sentences.en: The whole approach is called the forgiving road.
sentences.zh: 整个方法被称为“宽容道路”。

sentences.en: The idea was that, you know, to first try to minimize the potential that a crash could happen through,
sentences.zh: 其理念是，你知道，首先尽量减少通过以下方式发生碰撞的可能性：

sentences.en: again, through lack of obstacles, you know, generous sight lines, all these sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 同样，通过减少障碍物、宽阔的视线，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: But then if a crash did happen, to kind of mitigate the effects of what would happen,
sentences.zh: 但如果确实发生了碰撞，也要减轻碰撞后果，

sentences.en: to not punish the driver for the mistake that he will inevitably make.
sentences.zh: 不要因为司机不可避免会犯的错误而惩罚他们。

sentences.en: This was, I'm quoting some of the language from the time.
sentences.zh: 这是，我引用了当时的一些说法。

sentences.en: So you see that nowadays in things like in California, you'll have your guardrails that are sort of wire guardrails
sentences.zh: 所以你现在在加州等地会看到，护栏是那种钢丝护栏，

sentences.en: that if a car strikes that guardrail, it tends to catch on the guardrail rather than being bounced back out into traffic,
sentences.zh: 如果汽车撞上护栏，它往往会被护栏挂住，而不是被弹回车流中，

sentences.en: which causes another series of collisions.
sentences.zh: 从而引发一系列连环碰撞。

sentences.en: So this forgiving road is a positive thing in terms of good safety engineering.
sentences.zh: 所以这种“宽容道路”在良好的安全工程方面是一件积极的事情。

sentences.en: But they were so sort of seduced by it that the call was made to bring it into even the surface street network.
sentences.zh: 但他们被它迷住了，以至于决定将其引入地面街道网络。

sentences.en: So things like street trees began to be deemed hazards by engineers, just outright hazards.
sentences.zh: 于是，街道树木等事物开始被工程师视为危险，纯粹的危险。

sentences.en: I mean, and that makes sense on a high-speed country road.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在高速乡村公路上是有道理的。

sentences.en: But if you're talking about a residential street where you're not supposed to be going more than 25 anyway,
sentences.zh: 但如果你谈论的是一条限速本来就不超过25英里的住宅街道，

sentences.en: is the presence of a street tree on the side of the road where it's providing shade and comfort to pedestrians,
sentences.zh: 路边为行人提供遮荫和舒适感的树木，

sentences.en: you know, is that the same sort of hazard?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这算是同样的危险吗？

sentences.en: Is it even a hazard at all?
sentences.zh: 这甚至算得上是危险吗？

sentences.en: The conclusion many planners came to was, yes, trees are a hazard.
sentences.zh: 许多规划者得出的结论是：是的，树木是危险的。

sentences.en: You find pre-war suburbs, you have the street, a set of trees, and then the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 在战前的郊区，你会看到街道、一排树木，然后是人行道。

sentences.en: Post-war, this sort of shift began to happen where the trees were moved on the other side of the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 战后，这种转变开始发生，树木被移到了人行道的另一侧。

sentences.en: Suddenly, pedestrians were put into the position of being the buffer between drivers and those menacing trees.
sentences.zh: 突然间，行人被置于司机和那些威胁性的树木之间，充当了缓冲带。

sentences.en: It was sort of a pernicious thing that happened here is that, you know, as you move those trees away,
sentences.zh: 这里发生了一件相当有害的事情，就是，你知道，当你把那些树移走时，

sentences.en: the visual sensation of the road became wider.
sentences.zh: 道路的视觉感受变得更宽了。

sentences.en: And if there's one kind of iron law of traffic engineering, it gets into this visual perception thing as well.
sentences.zh: 如果说交通工程有一条铁律的话，它也涉及这种视觉感知。

sentences.en: The wider a road is or is perceived to be...
sentences.zh: 道路越宽，或者被认为越宽……

sentences.en: The faster driver speed tends to increase.
sentences.zh: 司机的车速往往就越快。

sentences.en: And of course, you know, the final, if you look at sort of 1990s era, you know, suburbia,
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，最后，如果你看看20世纪90年代的郊区，

sentences.en: that they just kind of eliminated the sidewalk and the trees altogether.
sentences.zh: 他们干脆把人行道和树木完全取消了。

sentences.en: So that was sort of the final solution, just eliminate any kind of hazard.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是最终的解决方案，消除任何形式的危险。

sentences.en: And Tom Vanderbilt says you can almost date a subdivision's development based on that shift.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·范德比尔特说，你几乎可以根据这种转变来判断一个住宅区的开发年代。

sentences.en: And this points to one of the problems about road engineering is that humans tend to consume
sentences.zh: 这指出了道路工程的一个问题，即人类倾向于消耗

sentences.en: the extra engineering measures that have been built in for their safety.
sentences.zh: 为他们的安全而内置的额外工程措施。

sentences.en: Much in the same way, I like to draw the analogy with some of the research that's been done on food
sentences.zh: 就像我喜欢用康奈尔大学布莱恩·万辛克（Brian Wansink）在食品包装方面所做的一些研究来做类比一样，

sentences.en: packaging by Brian Wanzik at Cornell University, doing experiments where, you know, if you give
sentences.zh: 他做了一些实验，你知道，如果你给

sentences.en: people, just random group people, large buckets of popcorn filled to the top with popcorn and
sentences.zh: 人们，随机的一群人，装满爆米花的大桶，然后

sentences.en: give them a smaller amount of popcorn in a smaller package, they'll just eat more of the larger
sentences.zh: 给他们较小包装的少量爆米花，他们会吃掉更多大包装的，

sentences.en: package, whether it has nothing to do with their level of hunger.
sentences.zh: 无论这与他们的饥饿程度是否有关。

sentences.en: It's just the size of the package influences their behavior.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是包装的大小影响了他们的行为。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of our road environments are sort of like that.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的许多道路环境也是如此。

sentences.en: They're over-engineered for the safety.
sentences.zh: 它们为了安全被过度设计了。

sentences.en: And then we tend to consume a lot of the extras, getting us back to this kind of homeostatic
sentences.zh: 然后我们往往会消耗掉很多额外的东西，让我们回到这种稳态，

sentences.en: edge that we're always kind of playing with, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们一直在这种边缘上徘徊。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible is Sam Greenspan and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 《99%隐形》由萨姆·格林斯潘（Sam Greenspan）和我，罗曼·马尔斯制作。

sentences.en: It's a project of 91.7 Local Public Radio, KALW in San Francisco, and the American Institute
sentences.zh: 它是旧金山91.7本地公共广播电台KALW和旧金山美国建筑师协会的一个项目。

sentences.en: of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并点赞我们的节目。

sentences.zh: 事实上，很多讨论和互动都是在那里发生的。

sentences.en: In fact, that's where a lot of the discussion and interaction happens.
sentences.zh: 所以请加入我们的Facebook页面。

sentences.en: So join us over on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我们快要达到10,000个赞了，我会非常高兴的。

sentences.zh: 我的推特账号是Roman Mars，我们在99percentinvisible.org上提供了本期节目中提到的所有内容的链接。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars, and we have links to all the stuff that we've been talking about
sentences.zh: 哦，还有一件事。

sentences.zh: 我和其他所有热爱音频创作的人都欠第三海岸国际音频节（Third Coast International Audio Festival）一个巨大的人情。

sentences.en: Oh, one more thing.
sentences.zh: 每年，我都会给他们寄点小礼物，确保他们能继续办下去。

sentences.en: I and every other creative audio lover owes a huge debt to the Third Coast International
sentences.zh: 或者我买一件T恤，他们拥有我全世界最喜欢的T恤设计，毫无疑问。

sentences.zh: 正面印着“听”这个词，用盲文书写。

sentences.zh: 我每种颜色都有六件。

sentences.zh: 这对任何广播爱好者来说都是必备品。
